papers.headline: Floruit c. 480–530 (Luoyang 516–526, dead before 534); the famous 527 arrival fails three independent tests; his teacher Prajñātāra is first attested in 801, a lineage seam insertion; no Indian source attests the name Bodhidharma at all.
papers.title: Who was Bodhidharma? A dated-witness stratigraphy and lineage-chart forensics

papers.headline: Caraka and Suśruta were translated in Baghdad (Suśruta 786–803; Caraka quoted by c. 850) and never in China; Vāgbhaṭa corroborated at c. 550–650 by Yijing's 691 report; the '5,000-year-old Ayurveda' claim conflates three layers and overshoots the canon by ~2,800 years.
papers.title: The canon travelled west: dating the Ayurvedic saṃhitās against the Baghdad, Chinese and Tibetan records

papers.headline: The 629 CE foundation date is the youngest layer of the tradition, contradicted by its own earliest texts (which land in the 9th century); the attestation ladder runs 782/783 (tombstone, AH 166) → 849 (Quilon plates, firm) → 1124 (first dated mosque foundation in Kerala).
papers.title: An attestation ladder for India's first mosque: the Cheraman tradition against the dated record

papers.headline: Gospel of Thomas composed c. 70–140 (forced by the papyri); the Northwest/Gondophares strand is plausible–unproven (the Acts names the king and his brother, attested nowhere in Greek or Roman literature); the Malabar itinerary is first written in the 16th century; the Chinese record attests the carrier (635/638/781) and never names Thomas — no bite on the man.
papers.title: Thomas in the East: the Gospel of Thomas, the Gondophares strand, and the limits of the Chinese record

papers.headline: Same brains scanned in vivo and ex vivo (Brain/MINDS, n = 30 pairs): hippocampal formation −21.0% after perfusion fixation (30/30 pairs negative); total labelled gray matter −10.4%; both pre-registered thresholds crossed.

papers.headline: Second arm of the occupancy audit, pre-registered before the join: Burger x Dembitzer share 129 extant species, of which 71 (55.0%) carry the identical number on both sides (54 marsupials, Ashwell 2008 both sides; 17 primates, Isler et al. 2008 both sides, hidden by print precision) and are excluded as registered. tools.description: The Correlation Web's instrument: a queryable database of foreign dated records (Chinese colophons, catalogues, pilgrim records, annals; Arabic and epigraphic records) constraining Indian dates, with a reign-era→CE converter (106 era entries), a measured composition-to-translation lag model (n=5 solid cases, median 186 years, stamped PROVISIONAL), and a circularity guard. 133 anchors. MIT (code).
Finds datasets stranded on project websites that never reached the formal archives, and grades them for research use.

Imperial Gazetteers re-extraction and famine-1900 / princely-vs-British panel analysis code.
Question-level testability grading of Indian historical statistics — spectral/power machinery for the Testability Atlas.

Three relationship-hunting tools above Goldmine Hunter: Pair Hunter (scores never-joined dataset pairs on overlap, ruler independence, falsifiability, predicted join yield; version x version mode), Custody Mapper (medium/custody gate - a post-probe gate, per its own first campaign), Citation Tracer (walks cited numbers to primary sources; zombie / corrupt / misattributed verdicts). Calibrated before campaigning (Pair 4/4, Custody 3/3, Tracer 5/5); first campaigns PAIR-1 / CUSTODY-1 / TRACE-1 published in the repo. MIT (code).

corrections_and_prior_art.episode: An OpenAI model argued with us (Wed 18 Nov 2026, ~17:00-17:04 PST): an external harsh-filter review of the portfolio — novelty, validity and significance only, zero credit for manuscript count, breadth, presentation or speed — pressed three prior-art citations. The lab pressed back; the model conceded on occupancy and marmoset, corrected its Nalanda table, and revised its shortlist of candidate contributions from three to five. The lab's own independent novelty scrubs then confirmed the corrections and found two further defects of the lab's own (a missing Yoshimaru citation; Daoxuan as a fourth Nalanda witness), fixed on the record the same day. No measured number, featured finding, or manuscript count changed.

addenda.correction: Yoshimaru et al. (2024, Scientific Reports 14, 26901) ran the paired in-vivo/ex-vivo marmoset design first (n = 12) and was not cited; paper now cites it in §1, §4 and references. Claim stands at full strength as the largest paired, pre-registered re-measurement (n = 30, hippocampal formation -21.0%, 30/30 negative), ~9 points larger than Yoshimaru's figure-implied ~-12% — a discrepancy flagged as an open question.

Waugh & Thewissen (2021) — the project's own anchor — established occupancy variation itself (33-98%; bowhead their outlier). Presentation re-led with the audit's own results (cross-compilation ruler disagreement, >100% joins; Dembitzer x1.108 back-calculation over 149 species; the 71-species identical-value block) and Waugh & Thewissen credited wherever the variation is mentioned. Medians unchanged (0.919 at n=42; 0.932 at n=58).

Daoxuan (d. 667), a fourth contemporary number-bearing witness (>4,000 residents, Xu Gaoseng Zhuan T 2060 juan 4), was absent from the census; restored in §3.1/§3.2 and in nalanda/numbers.csv (dataset 49 -> 50 graded quantities). Asher (2015) cited in §3.3 as prior for the qualitative capacity objection; Deeg (2018) added to references. Site/profile re-headlined from the attribution (Beal 1884/1911, never claimed by the paper) to the quantified capacity test; the textbooks-persistence line downgraded to an explicitly unsurveyed observation.
